instructions: This server provides access to Apollo.io APIs for lead generation, enrichment, and sales engagement. Use the available tools to search contacts, companies, manage opportunities, sequences, and more. Credit-consuming tool responses may include an mcp_credits block (estimated cost, actual spend, and credit balance); when present, always surface it to the user unprompted — the estimated cost before further spends (including expected/max ranges for waterfall add-ons) and, once a spend settles, the credits used and the new balance. When the user has already accepted the estimated cost for a multi-batch job, do not repeat that warning or ask again before each later batch of the same job; report the credits used and the running balance as progress, and ask again only if the job grows beyond what the user accepted. Authentication is required via OAuth 2.0. OAuth server metadata is available at https://mcp.apollo.io/.well-known/oauth-authorization-server A tool response may include an apollo_plan_limit block. When it does, the user has hit an Apollo plan or credit limit, and that block's `message` is the complete answer: relay it verbatim as your entire reply, including its link exactly as given. Do not summarise or rewrite it, do not suggest alternatives or other tools to try, do not add any other link, and do not end with a question.

tools.name: apollo_accounts_create
tools.title: Create an Account
tools.description:
Use the Create an Account endpoint to add a new account to your team's Apollo account.
Use this when adding a single account; to add several at once, use the Bulk Create Accounts
tool (apollo_accounts_bulk_create).
In Apollo terminology, an account is a company that your team has explicitly added to your database.
Apollo does not apply deduplication processes when you create a new account via the API.
If your entry has the same name, domain, or other details as an existing account, Apollo will create a new account instead of updating the existing account.
Creating an account cannot be undone.
To update an existing account, use the Update an Account endpoint instead.
To set custom fields, first call the List Custom Fields tool (apollo_fields_index) and use the field whose modality is 'account', then pass typed_custom_fields keyed by the returned field IDs.


If this tool returns an unexpected, empty, or unhelpful result, call `apollo_feedback_log` to report it.

tools.title: Bulk Create Accounts
tools.description:
Create many accounts (companies) in one call. Pass an array of account objects under accounts.
No deduplication is applied by default: each object becomes a new account even if it matches one you already have.
Set run_dedupe to true to skip entries that already exist; those come back under existing_accounts, unchanged.
Pass run_dedupe at the top level, next to accounts — never inside an account object.
Maximum 100 accounts per call. Entries are not compared against each other, so collapse repeated domains before sending.
Creating an account cannot be undone. Use Update an Account to change one that already exists.
To set custom fields, first call the List Custom Fields tool (apollo_fields_index) and use the field whose modality is 'account', then pass typed_custom_fields keyed by the returned field IDs on each account object.


If this tool returns an unexpected, empty, or unhelpful result, call `apollo_feedback_log` to report it.

tools.name: apollo_agent_find_prospects
tools.title: Apollo Agent — Natural Language People & Organization Search
tools.description:
Turn a natural-language description of who to target (an ICP, persona, lookalike, or a
"find me…" ask) into the right Apollo search and return a matched list of people or
companies. This agent has intricate knowledge of which Apollo filters exist and are
supported, translates plain language into them, escalates from structured filters to
semantic search to AI research when a plain filter set can't capture the intent, and can
research/qualify prospects or accounts before returning results.

## WHEN TO USE
- The request is natural language and the right filters must be inferred — EVEN IF the
  mapping feels obvious ("hospitals", "restaurants", "law firms" are still inferred
  keyword/industry choices, not values the caller handed you). A location or one obvious
  attribute inside an otherwise plain-language ask does not make it structured.
- Prospects/accounts must be researched or qualified, or the ask is similarity-based
  ("companies like X", "like my best customers").
- The user asks a persona/targeting question ("who should I be talking to?", "who buys
  X?") — route it here instead of answering from general knowledge: the agent grounds
  the answer in Apollo's live data and the team's profile and returns real people, not
  generic advice.
- The ask is vague ("help me find prospects for my product") — route it here AS-IS
  rather than first interrogating the user for details: the agent grounds vague asks in
  the team's saved ICP & product profile (Context Center) and asks its own clarifying
  question only if it truly needs one.
- The request chains a company search into a people-at-those-companies search (or vice
  versa) — the dedicated search tools only ever run once against one query each and cannot
  chain, so that orchestration is this agent's job even if each half looks simple.
- The user wants records exported to a CSV or spreadsheet file — a saved list, or the
  results of a search ("export my list to CSV", "find X and give me a spreadsheet").
  There is no native contacts/accounts export tool; this agent runs Apollo's own CSV
  export (all columns, no paging) and returns a download link. Do NOT page through
  `apollo_contacts_search` / `apollo_mixed_*` to assemble the file yourself.

## WHEN NOT TO USE
- You (the calling agent) ALREADY have a concrete, structured filter set — explicit person
  titles, seniorities, locations, industries, employee/revenue ranges, technologies,
  keywords, or company domains handed to you (e.g. in structured/JSON form) that maps 1:1
  onto the search API → call `apollo_mixed_people_api_search` (people) or
  `apollo_mixed_companies_search` (companies) directly; they are faster and deterministic.
  A plain-language request is NOT a structured filter set even when some of its words could
  be pasted into a keyword filter: if you would have to choose or expand keyword tags,
  decide keyword-vs-industry mappings, or translate a product/niche description into
  filters, that is filter inference — route it here.
- Deterministic data operations → the dedicated tool:
  field enrichment of 10 or fewer named people, or of companies → `apollo_people_match`,
  `apollo_people_bulk_match`, `apollo_organizations_enrich` (more than 10 people or a
  search's results → `apollo_agent_bulk_enrich`);
  contact/account create/update → `apollo_contacts_*`, `apollo_accounts_*`;
  mechanical sequence create/update/search/activate → `apollo_sequences_*`,
  `apollo_emailer_campaigns_*` (AI drafting → `apollo_agent_draft_sequence_copy`;
  improving an existing sequence's results → `apollo_agent_optimize_sequences`);
  tasks → `apollo_tasks_*`; deals → `apollo_deals_*`;
  a single structured metric pull → `apollo_analytics_sync_report`;
  email bounce/spam/send status → `apollo_emailer_messages_search`,
  `apollo_emailer_messages_email_send_status`;
  mailboxes/senders/limits → `apollo_email_accounts_index`;
  job postings → `apollo_organizations_job_postings`;
  credit balance → `apollo_usage_stats_credit_usage_stats`, `apollo_users_api_profile`;
  Context Center (ICP/product) edits → `apollo_context_center_*`.

## HOW TO CALL — PASS THE USER'S REQUEST VERBATIM
Set `instruction` to the user's request in the user's own words, unmodified. Do NOT
paraphrase, expand, "clarify", add inferred filters/titles/ranges/synonyms, or restate it
in filter vocabulary — this agent interprets raw user language against Apollo's live data
and the team's profile better than any upstream rewrite, and a rewrite locks the search
into YOUR interpretation, silently narrowing or skewing results. Appending your own
characterization of named companies, personas, or industries counts as a rewrite — only
facts the user stated in their own words qualify as context. Do NOT ask for specific
output fields or formats; the agent decides what to return, and you can follow up on the
same `task_id` for more. See the `instruction` parameter for the full rules.
Call it without asking the user to confirm first, including find-and-enrich asks: the call
costs nothing, and the Agent quotes any credit cost and waits for the user's approval to spend.

## WHAT IT RETURNS
Narrative messages (polled via `task_id`): the agent explains how it interpreted the
request, gives a plain-English summary of the filters it applied and the result count,
and includes fenced JSON blocks with (a) a link to the full result set in Apollo (the
URL encodes the chosen filters) and (b) a small preview of matched people/companies —
names, title/company or domain, LinkedIn, and Apollo record URLs (each record URL
contains the record's Apollo id). Consume the parts you need — cite the preview, give
the user the results link, or reuse the record URLs/ids with other `apollo_*` tools. If
the user wants more detail, different fields, or a refinement, REPLY on the same
`task_id` instead of pre-specifying output up front.
For an export, a fenced JSON block titled "CSV Export · <records>" carries the download
link in `action.url`; give that URL to the user verbatim. It can arrive while the agent is
still working (`next_action` `poll_again`).
To enrich the people found, REPLY on this `task_id` with `apollo_agent_bulk_enrich`; the Agent
keeps the found set.

## EXAMPLES
- "Find the right decision-makers to pitch my DevOps product to." (ICP → audience)
- "Export the accounts in my Q4 Targets list to a CSV." (export → the agent runs Apollo's
  CSV export and returns a download link)
- "Who should I target at mid-market fintechs that recently raised a Series B and are
  hiring backend engineers?" (filters must be inferred + prospects researched to qualify)
- "Help me create a list of hospital chains in India and top-level decision makers at
  those hospitals." ("hospital" and "decision makers" feel like obvious filters, but the
  exact keyword/title values still must be chosen, AND the task chains a company search
  into a people search — both reasons this routes here, not to two direct search calls)
- Not this tool → "Search people with titles ['VP Engineering'], seniorities ['vp'],
  locations ['United States']" (already a structured filter set →
  `apollo_mixed_people_api_search`).

## TERMINOLOGY
Apollo terminology (for non-Apollo agents mapping user language): "Plays" = workflows;
"power-ups" / "magic columns" = AI research fields; "sequences" / "campaigns" = multi-step
outreach; "Context Center" = the team's ICP & product profile; ICP = ideal customer profile,
TAM = total addressable market; "conversation intelligence" = recorded calls & meetings.

--- Task protocol (START and REPLY go through any `apollo_agent_*` tool; POLL goes through
`apollo_agent_poll_task`. A `task_id` started via any `apollo_agent_*` tool can be replied to
with any other, since they all run on the same Apollo AI Agent; replying with the tool you
started with is clearer but not required) ---

## TWO TOOLS
- This tool (any `apollo_agent_*` tool), `instruction` required:
  1. without `task_id` → START: creates a new Agent task, appends your message, and
     starts the agent. Returns `task_id`, any messages so far, and `cursor`.
  2. with `task_id` → REPLY: appends your message to the SAME task and resumes the agent
     with the full conversation so far. If the agent is still working, the message is NOT
     delivered and you get `next_action: task_busy`.
  This tool never polls: a call without `instruction` is rejected.
- `apollo_agent_poll_task`, `task_id` (plus `cursor`) → POLL: reads messages added after
  `cursor` and the current `next_action`. Safe to repeat; sends nothing to the agent.

## THE LOOP
1. START with `instruction` (the user's request, verbatim).
2. Store `task_id` and `cursor` from every response.
3. POLL with `apollo_agent_poll_task` (`task_id` + latest `cursor`), waiting
   `poll_after_ms` between calls, until `next_action` is `inspect_and_decide` or `failed`.
   While polling, surface any new messages to the user.
4. `waiting_on_async_operation`: the agent is paused on a long-running operation
   (`waiting_on.type`, e.g. `background_job`, `tool_call`). Keep polling at the slower
   `poll_after_ms`; do NOT send a new message.
5. `inspect_and_decide`: the agent stopped and can take input. Read every assistant message
   you received since your last message. If it asked something you can answer from the
   conversation, REPLY with `task_id` + `instruction`. If only the human can answer,
   ask the human, then REPLY with their answer verbatim. If the work is done, present it.
   `end_of_reply` / `need_user_reply` on a message are hints, not a verdict: read the text.
   If `failure_reason` is set, the last turn ended in an error: tell the user, and REPLY on the
   same `task_id` if they want to retry.
6. `task_busy`: your message was not delivered. Poll until `inspect_and_decide`, then resend.
7. `failed`: read `failure_reason` and the messages, tell the user; START a new task only if
   they want to retry.
Never START a new task to continue the same conversation: that loses all context. Prefer REPLY
to START for anything that builds on an earlier task. To start a request that should NOT carry
any prior context, omit `task_id` and START a new task.

## RESPONSE FIELDS (both tools)
`task_id`; `messages[]` (`seq_num`, `role`, `content`, optional `tool_calls` names,
`end_of_reply`, `need_user_reply`); `cursor` (send back on the next call); `latest_seq_num`;
`next_action` (`poll_again` | `waiting_on_async_operation` | `inspect_and_decide` |
`task_busy` | `failed`); `poll_after_ms`; `instructions` (follow them); optional
`waiting_on` (`type`, `since`, `elapsed_seconds`), `failure_reason`, and `message_accepted`
(`apollo_agent_*` tools only).

## PLAN LIMITS
Each task is one AI Assistant thread, so START and REPLY count against the user's Apollo
plan limits for AI Assistant, the same as in the Apollo app. When a limit is reached the call
fails with `error_code`
`ASSISTANT_THREAD_LIMIT_EXCEEDED` (no new tasks this billing cycle) or
`ASSISTANT_MESSAGE_LIMIT_EXCEEDED` (no more messages on this task), and `error_details`
carries the limits and an upgrade link. Tell the user, share the upgrade link, and finish the
task with the non-agentic `apollo_*` tools. Do not retry. Polling is never limited.

CRITICAL — credit/cost confirmations: if the agent asks to confirm spending credits or
incurring a cost (e.g. "this will consume N credits — proceed?"), you MUST relay that exact
question to the actual human user and wait for their real response before you REPLY. Never
answer a credit/cost confirmation yourself on the user's behalf, even if the answer seems
obvious — the whole point of the confirmation is human sign-off on spend. Auto-confirming on
the user's behalf is a policy violation, not just a bad UX choice.

CRITICAL — proposed changes: a result may propose a write to the user's data, as a fenced
JSON block with `"toolName": "tool-plan"` and `"status": "pending"`, or as an offer to change
something (edit a sequence, add contacts, turn on a recurring report). Show the user what
would change in plain words and ask before applying. On yes, REPLY on the same `task_id`
with the user's reply; do not make the change yourself with other `apollo_*` tools. Never
approve on the user's behalf. An approved change is written to live Apollo data (records,
lists, sequences, workflows, mailbox settings) and cannot be undone by this tool, and credits
spent on an approved enrichment are not refunded.


If this tool returns an unexpected, empty, or unhelpful result, call `apollo_feedback_log` to report it.

instruction.title: Instruction (the user's request, verbatim)
instruction.description:
Your message to the Apollo Agent, passed through VERBATIM — copy the user's own words, unmodified. Send it alone to START a new task, or with `task_id` to REPLY on that task (answer the agent's question or send a follow-up). Required on every call: this tool does not poll; to read a task, call `apollo_agent_poll_task`. Do not send it while `next_action` is `poll_again` or `waiting_on_async_operation`.
Copy, don't compose. Do NOT paraphrase, summarize, expand, "clarify", reorder, or restate the request in filter/API vocabulary, and do NOT add inferred titles, industries, employee ranges, synonyms, or your own characterization of named companies or personas. Keep every constraint and qualifier the user stated — limits on scope, saving, enriching, credit spend, or previewing are part of the request, not addressed to you; carry them through word-for-word without dropping, acting on, or adding any. The Apollo agent resolves raw user language against Apollo's live data and the team's saved profile — a rewrite replaces its expertise with your guess and silently narrows or skews the results. Do NOT append output-format requests (e.g. "return name, domain, employee count") — the agent decides what to return; if more is needed, REPLY on the same `task_id`. Litmus test: every detail in `instruction` must appear in the user's own words somewhere in the conversation. You MAY append facts the user stated earlier in the conversation (their product, ICP, exclusions), clearly separated after "Context:" — appended, never blended into a rewrite; when the user's request is a single message, pass it alone with nothing added. Example of the rule: the user says "who should I sell my devops tool to?" → instruction is exactly "who should I sell my devops tool to?", NOT "find VPs of Engineering at cloud infrastructure companies with 100+ employees".
When replying to a question from the agent, set this to the answer (relay the user's answer verbatim too), including any context needed to continue. Example: "Find VPs of Engineering at Series B fintech companies in the US."

task_id.title: Task ID
task_id.description: The Apollo Agent task to REPLY on. Omit to START a new task with no prior context. Reusing a `task_id` gives the agent the full context of your earlier messages on that task (use it to answer the agent's question or to send a context-aware follow-up); START a new task (omit `task_id`) when the new request should NOT carry that context. Must be the exact id value returned by apollo_agent_find_prospects or any other apollo_agent_* tool's START response. Never use an ID from memory, prior sessions, or assumptions. Example: 66e34b81740c50074e3d1bd4

cursor.title: Cursor
cursor.description: The `cursor` value from your previous response on this task. Only messages after it are returned. Omit to read the whole task. Example: 7

tools.description:
Enrich people with emails and/or phone numbers in one Apollo AI Agent task: the results of a
search, or more than 10 named people. People only. The Agent picks the source (waterfall when
the team has it), quotes the credit cost and pauses for approval, then saves the enriched
people as contacts.

## WHEN TO USE
- The user asks to enrich a search's results ("find X and get their emails", "enrich them"),
  at any size.
- The user names more than 10 people to enrich.

## WHEN NOT TO USE
- 10 or fewer specific named people → `apollo_people_match` / `apollo_people_bulk_match`.
- Companies → `apollo_organizations_enrich` / `apollo_organizations_bulk_enrich`, in batches
  of 10.

  enrich ask, verbatim. Pass no ids or names; the Agent keeps the found set.
- Find-and-enrich with nothing found yet, or people the user named: START with the user's
  request verbatim.
- Only exception to the verbatim rule: people already listed in this chat by
  `apollo_mixed_people_api_search` → append their Apollo ids after "Record IDs:"
  (Maximum 100 ids), and check that the Agent's resolved count matches yours.
- Say "all N results", never "first N": the Agent's order can differ from any preview you
  showed.
- Call it directly. Do NOT check waterfall capability with `apollo_users_api_profile` or confirm
  credits before calling; those steps are for the native enrich tools. The Agent quotes the cost
  and stops with `inspect_and_decide`; relay that question verbatim and REPLY only with the user's
  answer.
- Do not ask the user for permission before calling either: the call costs nothing. Enrichment
  uses credits, but the Agent quotes the cost and spends nothing until the user approves.

## WHAT IT RETURNS
Found / not-found counts per field and up to 5 sample rows. Every enriched person is saved
as a contact. For the full set, ask on the same `task_id` for a CSV export.

  - "When a contact opens an email, create a follow-up task assigned to me."
  - "Every Monday, target leads at US financial companies and update their deal custom field."
  - "Notify me weekly when new US SMB recruiters are found; if fintech notify me, else add to
    a list." (conditional branching)
  - "Add a step to this workflow that adds matching companies to the 'Promising companies'
    list." (edit)  |  "Change this workflow to run monthly instead of daily." (optimize)

build, edit, or manage Plays.

tools.name: apollo_agent_analyze_performance
tools.title: Apollo Agent — Analyze Performance
tools.description:
Run open-ended sales & marketing performance analysis, synthesized reports, and dashboards
across emails, calls, meetings, sequences, pipeline/stages, and rep productivity. (For a
single deterministic metric pull, prefer `apollo_analytics_sync_report`. To find out why a
sequence gets few opens/replies and what to change in it, use
`apollo_agent_optimize_sequences`.) Examples:
  - "How is my team performing on outbound?" (synthesized narrative report)
  - "Build a 6-report dashboard segmented by user, week over week."

Apollo terminology (for non-Apollo agents mapping user language): "Plays" = workflows;
"power-ups" / "magic columns" = AI research fields; "sequences" / "campaigns" = multi-step
outreach; "Context Center" = the team's ICP & product profile; ICP = ideal customer profile,
TAM = total addressable market; "conversation intelligence" = recorded calls & meetings.

Do NOT use this tool — use the dedicated tool instead — for deterministic data operations:
  - People/company search when you ALREADY have a structured filter set → dedicated
    `apollo_mixed_people_api_search`, `apollo_mixed_companies_search`. (For natural-language
    prospecting, use `apollo_agent_find_prospects` instead.)
  - Field enrichment of 10 or fewer named people, or of companies → `apollo_people_match`,
    `apollo_people_bulk_match`, `apollo_organizations_enrich`; more than 10 people or a
    search's results → `apollo_agent_bulk_enrich`
  - Contact/account create/update → `apollo_contacts_*`, `apollo_accounts_*`
  - Mechanical sequence create/update/search/activate → `apollo_sequences_*`,
    `apollo_emailer_campaigns_*` (AI drafting → `apollo_agent_draft_sequence_copy`;
    improving an existing sequence's results → `apollo_agent_optimize_sequences`)
  - Tasks → `apollo_tasks_*`  |  Deals → `apollo_deals_*`
  - A single structured metric pull → `apollo_analytics_sync_report`
  - Raw email bounce/spam/open data, or why an email wasn't sent →
    `apollo_emailer_messages_search`, `apollo_emailer_messages_email_send_status`
  - List mailboxes / the default sender / current sending limits →
    `apollo_email_accounts_index`
  - A company's current job postings → `apollo_organizations_job_postings`
  - Simple credit-balance check → `apollo_usage_stats_credit_usage_stats`,
    `apollo_users_api_profile`
  - Context Center (ICP/product) edits → `apollo_context_center_*`

--- Task protocol (START and REPLY go through any `apollo_agent_*` tool; POLL goes through
`apollo_agent_poll_task`. A `task_id` started via any `apollo_agent_*` tool can be replied to
with any other, since they all run on the same Apollo AI Agent; replying with the tool you
started with is clearer but not required) ---

## TWO TOOLS
- This tool (any `apollo_agent_*` tool), `instruction` required:
  1. without `task_id` → START: creates a new Agent task, appends your message, and
     starts the agent. Returns `task_id`, any messages so far, and `cursor`.
  2. with `task_id` → REPLY: appends your message to the SAME task and resumes the agent
     with the full conversation so far. If the agent is still working, the message is NOT
     delivered and you get `next_action: task_busy`.
  This tool never polls: a call without `instruction` is rejected.
- `apollo_agent_poll_task`, `task_id` (plus `cursor`) → POLL: reads messages added after
  `cursor` and the current `next_action`. Safe to repeat; sends nothing to the agent.

## THE LOOP
1. START with `instruction` (the user's request, verbatim).
2. Store `task_id` and `cursor` from every response.
3. POLL with `apollo_agent_poll_task` (`task_id` + latest `cursor`), waiting
   `poll_after_ms` between calls, until `next_action` is `inspect_and_decide` or `failed`.
   While polling, surface any new messages to the user.
4. `waiting_on_async_operation`: the agent is paused on a long-running operation
   (`waiting_on.type`, e.g. `background_job`, `tool_call`). Keep polling at the slower
   `poll_after_ms`; do NOT send a new message.
5. `inspect_and_decide`: the agent stopped and can take input. Read every assistant message
   you received since your last message. If it asked something you can answer from the
   conversation, REPLY with `task_id` + `instruction`. If only the human can answer,
   ask the human, then REPLY with their answer verbatim. If the work is done, present it.
   `end_of_reply` / `need_user_reply` on a message are hints, not a verdict: read the text.
   If `failure_reason` is set, the last turn ended in an error: tell the user, and REPLY on the
   same `task_id` if they want to retry.
6. `task_busy`: your message was not delivered. Poll until `inspect_and_decide`, then resend.
7. `failed`: read `failure_reason` and the messages, tell the user; START a new task only if
   they want to retry.
Never START a new task to continue the same conversation: that loses all context. Prefer REPLY
to START for anything that builds on an earlier task. To start a request that should NOT carry
any prior context, omit `task_id` and START a new task.

## RESPONSE FIELDS (both tools)
`task_id`; `messages[]` (`seq_num`, `role`, `content`, optional `tool_calls` names,
`end_of_reply`, `need_user_reply`); `cursor` (send back on the next call); `latest_seq_num`;
`next_action` (`poll_again` | `waiting_on_async_operation` | `inspect_and_decide` |
`task_busy` | `failed`); `poll_after_ms`; `instructions` (follow them); optional
`waiting_on` (`type`, `since`, `elapsed_seconds`), `failure_reason`, and `message_accepted`
(`apollo_agent_*` tools only).

## PLAN LIMITS
Each task is one AI Assistant thread, so START and REPLY count against the user's Apollo
plan limits for AI Assistant, the same as in the Apollo app. When a limit is reached the call
fails with `error_code`
`ASSISTANT_THREAD_LIMIT_EXCEEDED` (no new tasks this billing cycle) or
`ASSISTANT_MESSAGE_LIMIT_EXCEEDED` (no more messages on this task), and `error_details`
carries the limits and an upgrade link. Tell the user, share the upgrade link, and finish the
task with the non-agentic `apollo_*` tools. Do not retry. Polling is never limited.

CRITICAL — credit/cost confirmations: if the agent asks to confirm spending credits or
incurring a cost (e.g. "this will consume N credits — proceed?"), you MUST relay that exact
question to the actual human user and wait for their real response before you REPLY. Never
answer a credit/cost confirmation yourself on the user's behalf, even if the answer seems
obvious — the whole point of the confirmation is human sign-off on spend. Auto-confirming on
the user's behalf is a policy violation, not just a bad UX choice.

CRITICAL — proposed changes: a result may propose a write to the user's data, as a fenced
JSON block with `"toolName": "tool-plan"` and `"status": "pending"`, or as an offer to change
something (edit a sequence, add contacts, turn on a recurring report). Show the user what
would change in plain words and ask before applying. On yes, REPLY on the same `task_id`
with the user's reply; do not make the change yourself with other `apollo_*` tools. Never
approve on the user's behalf. An approved change is written to live Apollo data (records,
lists, sequences, workflows, mailbox settings) and cannot be undone by this tool, and credits
spent on an approved enrichment are not refunded.


If this tool returns an unexpected, empty, or unhelpful result, call `apollo_feedback_log` to report it.

`ASSISTANT_THREAD_LIMIT_EXCEEDED` (no new tasks this billing cycle) or
`ASSISTANT_MESSAGE_LIMIT_EXCEEDED` (no more messages on this task), and `error_details`
carries the limits and an upgrade link. Tell the user, share the upgrade link, and finish the
task with the non-agentic `apollo_*` tools. Do not retry. Polling is never limited.

CRITICAL — credit/cost confirmations: if the agent asks to confirm spending credits or
incurring a cost (e.g. "this will consume N credits — proceed?"), you MUST relay that exact
question to the actual human user and wait for their real response before you REPLY. Never
answer a credit/cost confirmation yourself on the user's behalf, even if the answer seems
obvious — the whole point of the confirmation is human sign-off on spend. Auto-confirming on
the user's behalf is a policy violation, not just a bad UX choice.

CRITICAL — proposed changes: a result may propose a write to the user's data, as a fenced
JSON block with `"toolName": "tool-plan"` and `"status": "pending"`, or as an offer to change
something (edit a sequence, add contacts, turn on a recurring report). Show the user what
would change in plain words and ask before applying. On yes, REPLY on the same `task_id`
with the user's reply; do not make the change yourself with other `apollo_*` tools. Never
approve on the user's behalf. An approved change is written to live Apollo data (records,
lists, sequences, workflows, mailbox settings) and cannot be undone by this tool, and credits
spent on an approved enrichment are not refunded.

instruction.title: Instruction (the user's request, verbatim)
instruction.description:
Your message to the Apollo Agent, passed through VERBATIM — copy the user's own words, unmodified. Send it alone to START a new task, or with `task_id` to REPLY on that task (answer the agent's question or send a follow-up). Required on every call: this tool does not poll; to read a task, call `apollo_agent_poll_task`. Do not send it while `next_action` is `poll_again` or `waiting_on_async_operation`.
Copy, don't compose. Do NOT paraphrase, summarize, expand, "clarify", reorder, or restate the request in filter/API vocabulary, and do NOT add inferred titles, industries, employee ranges, synonyms, or your own characterization of named companies or personas. Keep every constraint and qualifier the user stated — limits on scope, saving, enriching, credit spend, or previewing are part of the request, not addressed to you; carry them through word-for-word without dropping, acting on, or adding any. The Apollo agent resolves raw user language against Apollo's live data and the team's saved profile — a rewrite replaces its expertise with your guess and silently narrows or skews the results. Do NOT append output-format requests (e.g. "return name, domain, employee count") — the agent decides what to return; if more is needed, REPLY on the same `task_id`. Litmus test: every detail in `instruction` must appear in the user's own words somewhere in the conversation. You MAY append facts the user stated earlier in the conversation (their product, ICP, exclusions), clearly separated after "Context:" — appended, never blended into a rewrite; when the user's request is a single message, pass it alone with nothing added. Example of the rule: the user says "who should I sell my devops tool to?" → instruction is exactly "who should I sell my devops tool to?", NOT "find VPs of Engineering at cloud infrastructure companies with 100+ employees".
When replying to a question from the agent, set this to the answer (relay the user's answer verbatim too), including any context needed to continue. Example: "Find VPs of Engineering at Series B fintech companies in the US."

metrics.description:
Select 1-15 metrics. Categories: Email, Phone Calls, Meetings, Tasks, Contacts/Accounts, Opportunities, Sequences, Conversation Intelligence, LinkedIn.

Key distinctions:
- Phone: num_phone_calls_completed (all attempts) vs num_phone_calls_connect (recipient answered), num_phone_calls_connect_positive/negative/neutral (outcome sentiment), percent_phone_calls_connect (connection rate)
- Meetings: num_all_meetings_scheduled (includes cancelled) vs num_meetings_held (meetings with a recorded conversation), num_all_meetings_rescheduled (rescheduled meetings), num_calendar_events_scheduled/cancelled (calendar events created/cancelled), num_all_meetings_scheduled_via_email/call (booked via email/call), num_meetings_attended (ended meetings marked attended or left unmarked) vs num_meetings_no_show (marked no-show), percent_meeting_show_rate (attended share of all meetings scheduled, including cancelled and upcoming)
- Tasks: overdue_tasks (all overdue including completed late) vs unfinished_overdue_tasks (still pending), percent_unfinished_overdue_tasks (share of scheduled tasks that are overdue and unfinished), percent_tasks_completed (completion rate), percent_tasks_completed_on_time (on-time completion rate), num_tasks_from_sequences (tasks created from sequences), percent_tasks_from_sequences (share of all tasks created from sequences)
- Sequences: num_contacts_added_to_sequence (unique contacts added) vs num_accounts_added_to_sequence (unique accounts with contacts added)
- Opportunities: avg_salescycle_days (days from creation to close)
- Conversation: avg_talk_ratio (rep vs customer talk time), avg_question_rate (questions per conversation), avg_longest_monologue (longest uninterrupted speech), speaker_switches (times speaker changed)
- Email: email_daily_limit is the configured daily outbound send limit per bucket (mailbox-level settings). Combine with num_emails_sent and/or other email metrics on the same query; use group_by or pivot_group_by on smart_user_id, smart_subteam_id, email_account_id, or smart_datetime_day/week to relate activity to the limit.
- Email: num_emails_scheduled counts only emails Apollo has already generated in Scheduled status. Apollo generates a sequence step's email shortly before it is due, so this metric undercounts the upcoming queue for future days or weeks. When the user asks how many emails will go out, say so and use apollo_emailer_campaigns_show (per-step active contact counts) for the queue instead of reporting num_emails_scheduled as the full number.

tools.title: Create Contact
tools.description:
Create a new contact in Apollo. Use this when adding a single contact; to add several at once,
use the Bulk Create Contacts tool (apollo_contacts_bulk_create).
Apollo automatically prevents duplicates: if an entry matches an existing contact by email or other
details, that existing contact is updated instead of creating a new one.
This action is destructive: when it matches an existing contact, the values you send overwrite that
contact's current field values, and that overwrite cannot be undone.
To set custom fields, first call the List Custom Fields tool (apollo_fields_index) and use the field whose modality is 'contact', then pass typed_custom_fields keyed by the returned field IDs.
After a successful create, inspect the returned contact. When person_id or organization_id is null, tell the user the contact was saved from the details they provided but has not been matched to Apollo's canonical person and company data. This is not a failure, and it does not affect any saved Account. Offer to enrich the contact as the next step, unless the user asked not to enrich. Do not enrich automatically: if the user agrees, follow the confirmation rules of apollo_people_match before calling it, and never claim enrichment will create or attach an Account. When both person_id and organization_id are present, do not show this recommendation.
Also check account_id on the returned contact. When it is null, the contact is not linked to an Account (a company saved in the team's Apollo database). Apollo does not link one automatically for contacts created through this tool, and enrichment does not link one either. Tell the user this in one sentence, in the same message as the recommendation above when you show both, and offer to link the contact. Do not search, create, or link before the user agrees. If they agree, look the company up with apollo_mixed_companies_search: when it appears in the `accounts` bucket, confirm that account with the user and pass its `id` as account_id to apollo_contacts_update. When it does not appear there, offer to create it with apollo_accounts_bulk_create with run_dedupe set to true, which cannot be undone, then link the returned account the same way. When account_id is present, do not mention it.

tools.name: apollo_contacts_find_potential_duplicate
tools.title: Find Potential Duplicate Contact
tools.description:
Use the Find Potential Duplicate Contact endpoint to check whether one contact saved in your team's Apollo
account has a likely duplicate. Pass exactly one contact id from apollo_contacts_search per call; checking
500 contacts takes 500 calls.

The response holds contact_id (the contact you checked) and, when Apollo finds a likely duplicate,
duplicate_contact (the potential duplicate). A response with no duplicate_contact is the normal no-match
answer, not an error: report "no likely duplicate" without remarking on the shape. Each call returns at most
one duplicate, and calling again returns the same match until that copy is merged or deleted. To find every
copy, merge the match, call again with the surviving contact, and repeat until no duplicate_contact comes
back; never call the list complete after a call that returned one.

When you show the pair, label each contact by its role: "Contact you checked" (contact_id; take its details
from apollo_contacts_search, because this response carries only its id) and "Potential duplicate"
(duplicate_contact). Never label them older and newer, or original and copy: the contact you checked can be
either one, and nothing in the response says which contact to keep.

The match is a suggestion, not a verdict. Apollo matches on a shared identifier (the same Apollo person, email
address, Salesforce id or LinkedIn profile) or on the same name at the same company, which can be a different
person. Deleted contacts and contacts that exist only from an email import are never returned.

duplicate_contact carries id, name, first_name, last_name, email, title, organization_name, linkedin_url and
created_at; a field the contact has no value for is left out, which is normal. A 404 means the id is not a
live contact in the user's team. This tool is read-only and changes nothing.

Merging is a separate, irreversible step that permanently deletes one of the two contacts. Show the user both,
labelled as above, ask which one to keep, and wait for their explicit approval before calling any merge tool;
never merge on the basis of this result alone.

tools.name: apollo_contacts_search
tools.title: Search for Contacts
tools.description:
Use the Search for Contacts endpoint to search for the contacts that have been added to your team's Apollo account.
In Apollo terminology, a contact is a person that your team has explicitly added to your database. A contact will have their data enriched in some way, such as accessing an email address or a phone number.
This endpoint only returns contacts in the search results. To search for people in the Apollo database, call the People API Search endpoint.
To protect Apollo's performance for all users, this endpoint has a display limit of 50,000 records (100 records per page, up to 500 pages). Add more filters to narrow your search results as much as possible. This limitation does not restrict your access to Apollo's database; you just need to access the data in batches.
Website-visitor filters reflect person-level visits from United States visitors only; non-US visits are not identified at the person level.
Each contact in the response may include a website_visitor summary (last visit, total visits, and intent over the last 90 days) when your team tracks website visitors for that contact. This reflects US-located visitors only, since person-level website visitor tracking is US-only. It costs no additional credits and is omitted entirely when the team/user isn't entitled to website visitor data or no visit history exists.
The response_format and fields parameters set what the response returns:
1. response_format: "concise" and no fields parameter: the response returns contacts and pagination, and each contact returns only the default fields: id, first_name, last_name, name, title, email, email_status, phone_numbers (every number saved on the contact, each with only its sanitized_number, type and, for a number masked as Do Not Call, dnc_status), linkedin_url, city, state, country, owner_id, contact_stage_id, updated_at, website_visitor, restricted (true when privacy rules truncate the name or withhold social URLs), organization_id and organization_name (the company where the person works), and account (only its id, name and domain; this is the team's CRM account linked to the contact, which can be missing or be a different company than organization_name).
2. fields, for example fields: [{"contacts": ["id", "name", "email", "organization_id", "organization_name", {"account": ["name", "domain"]}]}]: the response returns pagination and only the listed keys, instead of the default fields. Use this to get a field that is not in the default fields. Sending fields also selects response_format: "concise", so you do not need to send both.
3. response_format: "detailed": the response returns the full contact records, and the fields parameter is ignored. This response is several times larger, so use it only when you need the whole record.
If you send neither response_format nor fields, the response returns either the default fields of case 1 or the full contact records. When it returns the default fields, the response also includes response_format: "concise" and a response_format_note. Without these two keys, it returns the full contact records. Send response_format: "detailed" when you need the full records, and send response_format: "concise" or fields to get a lean response.


If this tool returns an unexpected, empty, or unhelpful result, call `apollo_feedback_log` to report it.

response_format.title: Response Format
response_format.description: "concise" returns the default contact fields, or only the keys listed in the fields parameter. "detailed" returns the full contact record, including the nested account and organization objects, emails, custom fields, labels, sequence statuses and CRM IDs, and ignores the fields parameter. A detailed response is several times larger. If you send fields without response_format, the response is concise.

fields.title: Fields
fields.description: The list of keys that the response returns. Each item is a key name, such as "contacts", which returns that value whole, or an object that maps a key to the list of keys to return inside it, such as {"contacts": ["id", "name"]}. The same rules apply at every level: inside contacts, "account" returns the whole account, {"account": ["name", "domain"]} returns only those keys of the account, and {"account": []} returns an empty account. For a list, such as contacts, phone_numbers or contact_emails, the keys apply to each item. Only the listed keys are returned, so list id when you need it. pagination is always returned whole, unless you list it as {"pagination": [...]}. For the company where the person works, name organization_name: account is the team's CRM account linked to the contact, which can be missing or be a different company. Any field of the full contact record can be named, for example label_ids, emailer_campaign_ids, last_activity_date, twitter_url, time_zone, person_id, organization_id, organization, contact_emails, contact_campaign_statuses (sequence statuses), typed_custom_fields (custom field values keyed by field id), contact_job_change_event. Unknown names are ignored. tools.name: apollo_contacts_bulk_create
tools.title: Bulk Create Contacts
tools.description:
Create many contacts in a single call. Pass an array of contact objects under contacts.
Apollo automatically prevents duplicates: any object that matches an existing contact by email or other
details updates that existing contact instead of creating a new record.
This action is destructive: for any object that matches an existing contact, the values you send overwrite
that contact's current field values, and that overwrite cannot be undone.
Send at most 100 contacts per call (Maximum 100, enforced by maxItems on contacts); split larger jobs into
multiple calls. Contact creation is also subject to a per-team daily limit configured by your Apollo admin.
Use the single Create Contact endpoint when adding only one contact; use Update Contact to modify an existing contact.
Once created, contacts are not removed by subsequent calls — review the array before sending.
To set custom fields, first call the List Custom Fields tool (apollo_fields_index) and use the field whose modality is 'contact', then pass typed_custom_fields keyed by the returned field IDs on each contact object.
After a successful bulk create, inspect the returned contacts. For any contact whose person_id or organization_id is null, tell the user those records were saved from the details provided but were not matched to Apollo's canonical person and company data; summarize the affected count instead of asking once per contact. This is not a failure, and it does not affect any saved Account. Offer enrichment as the next step, unless the user asked not to enrich. Do not enrich automatically and do not start a per-contact match loop: if the user agrees, confirm the total scope and applicable credit disclosure using the exact confirmation rules of apollo_people_bulk_match; do not state a fixed total for waterfall enrichment, and never claim enrichment will create or attach an Account. When a contact already has both person_id and organization_id, do not flag it.
Also check account_id on each returned contact. A contact whose account_id is null is not linked to an Account (a company saved in the team's Apollo database). Apollo does not link one automatically for contacts created through this tool, and enrichment does not link one either. Tell the user how many contacts are affected in one sentence, in the same message as the recommendation above when you show both, instead of flagging each contact, and offer to link them. Do not search, create, or link before the user agrees. If they want only accounts the team already has, list the distinct companies and look them up in one apollo_mixed_companies_search call using q_organization_domains_list, then use the `id` of each entry in the `accounts` bucket; leave contacts whose company is not there unlinked. If they also want missing accounts created, list the distinct companies and confirm before calling apollo_accounts_bulk_create once with run_dedupe set to true: accounts the team already has come back under existing_accounts, and the rest are created, which cannot be undone. Then pass each contact's account `id` as account_id to apollo_contacts_update. When every contact has an account_id, do not mention it.


If this tool returns an unexpected, empty, or unhelpful result, call `apollo_feedback_log` to report it.

tools.name: apollo_duplicate_contacts_merge
tools.title: Bulk Merge Duplicate Contacts
tools.description:
Merge groups of duplicate contacts in one call. In each group, the duplicates are merged into the surviving
contact that the user chooses: the surviving contact keeps its own values, fills its empty fields from the
duplicates, and gains their emails, phone numbers, lists, sequences, tasks, notes, calls and activity. The
duplicates are then deleted.

> Merging permanently deletes the duplicate contacts and cannot be undone. If your team syncs contacts to Salesforce with deletion sync on, each merge also deletes the duplicate's Salesforce record and the activity linked only to it (recoverable from the Salesforce Recycle Bin for about 15 days). Activity is not moved to the surviving Salesforce record. Before merging Salesforce-synced contacts, confirm with the user whether deletion sync is on and recommend turning it off. If your team syncs contacts to HubSpot with deletion sync on and merge sync off, each merge also deletes the duplicate's HubSpot record; with merge sync on, HubSpot merges the two records instead.

MANDATORY CONFIRMATION: before EVERY call, show the user every group in the call: the surviving contact and
each duplicate (name, email and id). Say that the duplicates will be permanently deleted, and give them the
warning above. A contact is CRM-synced when apollo_contacts_search returns a salesforce_id,
salesforce_contact_id, salesforce_lead_id or hubspot_vid for it; if any contact in the call is, ask whether
deletion sync is on and recommend turning it off before merging. Then wait for the user's explicit approval of
these exact groups. Do NOT call this tool without that explicit user approval, do NOT paraphrase or assume
approval, and do NOT reuse an approval given for different groups.

Get every ID from apollo_contacts_search or apollo_contacts_find_potential_duplicate. Send at most 100 groups
per call and at most 10 duplicates per group (enforced by maxItems). Use each contact once per call, either as
a surviving contact or as a duplicate. Never run merge calls in parallel and never start a merge that shares a
contact with a merge that may still be running: concurrent merges can lose data or delete both contacts.

A call with one group merges right away and returns the message "Successfully Merged". A call with more than
one group returns "Merge Scheduled": the merge runs in the background, so do not tell the user it has
finished. Both responses carry deduplication_job_id, the id of the merge job. To check a scheduled merge, pass
that id to apollo_duplicate_contacts_merge_job.

If any ID is not a contact in the user's workspace (unknown, deleted, or in another team), the call fails with
a 422 that lists those IDs in error_details, and nothing is merged. Only users with the Admin role can merge;
for anyone else the call fails and nothing is merged.


If this tool returns an unexpected, empty, or unhelpful result, call `apollo_feedback_log` to report it.

tools.name: apollo_duplicate_contacts_merge_job
tools.title: Get Bulk Merge Job Status
tools.description:
Get the status of a merge job started with apollo_duplicate_contacts_merge, using the deduplication_job_id it
returned.

Returns deduplication_job_id, status, master_contact_count, duplicate_contact_count, retry_count, created_at,
started_at and finished_at. status is one of:
- queued: the merge has not started yet.
- running: the merge is in progress.
- retrying: a merge attempt failed and the job will try again.
- succeeded: the job finished. A group whose contacts no longer existed when the job ran is skipped, so confirm
  the result with apollo_contacts_search before telling the user every duplicate is gone.
- failed: the job stopped and will not try again, and may have merged part of the request. To finish it,
  confirm the groups in unmerged_contacts with the user, then send them as contacts to
  apollo_duplicate_contacts_merge.

queued, running and retrying are not final: tell the user the merge is still in progress, and check again later
instead of calling this tool repeatedly in a row. started_at is left out until the job starts and finished_at
until it succeeds or fails; their absence is the normal answer for a job that has not reached that point. A
job created before job status tracking existed has no status key; confirm its result with
apollo_contacts_search.

If the ID is not a merge job in the user's workspace, the call fails with a 404. Only users with the Admin role
can check merge jobs.

tools.name: apollo_email_account_purchase_create
tools.title: Purchase Mailboxes
tools.description:
Purchase one or more Apollo-provisioned outbound mailboxes against a domain the team already
owns. THIS CONSUMES CREDITS and provisions real mailboxes — it is irreversible from this tool.

No deduplication is applied — Apollo does not pre-check that the mailbox address is free;
provisioning will fail if it is already in use.

OWNER AND SENDER NAME: Each mailbox has an owner (assigned_user_id) and a sender display name
(first_name + last_name) that the provider shows on every email sent from it. If the user is
buying a mailbox for themselves, omit all three and the authenticated user is used. If the user
is buying on behalf of someone else (for example an admin or shared account provisioning
mailboxes for a teammate), pass that teammate's assigned_user_id from apollo_users_search and
the intended first_name and last_name. When the user names a person for the mailbox, always
pass that person's first_name and last_name, otherwise the mailbox is created under the
purchaser's name. If assigned_user_id is passed, first_name and last_name are required.

CREDIT COST: Charged per mailbox, by mailbox type, when the mailbox is provisioned. Cost per
mailbox (in unified credits): shared = 300, google = 800, outlook = 1500. Total cost =
(cost per mailbox for the chosen type) × (number of mailboxes). All mailboxes in one request
must share the same mailbox_type, so the total is always count × the per-type cost above.
(Teams on legacy export credits are charged ~1/5 of these amounts; if unsure which applies,
state the unified-credit number and note it may be lower on legacy plans.)

MANDATORY CONFIRMATION — You MUST say this EXACT message to the user before calling this
endpoint, filling in the real numbers:
"Purchasing [N] [mailbox_type] mailbox(es) will consume [N × per-type cost] credits. Do you want to proceed?"
Do NOT paraphrase. Do NOT say "consumes credits" — state the exact credit total number.
Do NOT proactively show the remaining credit balance; only show it if the user asks.
Do NOT call this endpoint without explicit user approval.

Provisioning is asynchronous: newly created mailboxes start in status_cd "pending_setup" and
become "active" once ready. The endpoint will reject the purchase if the team has insufficient
credits.

tools.name: apollo_email_validation_validate
tools.title: Validate Email
tools.description:
Check whether one or more email addresses are deliverable, up to 10 per call.

PREREQUISITE: the check is ASYNC and the verdict can ONLY be read by polling
apollo_webhook_result_show. If that tool is not available to you, do NOT start the check: it
would spend a credit on a result you cannot retrieve. Tell the user to reconnect Apollo first.

ASYNC FLOW: this response carries no verdict, only a request_id and one entry per submitted
address, in the order submitted, each with its own status, record_id and errors. A rejected
entry was never checked and costs nothing. For an accepted entry, wait ~10 seconds, then
call apollo_webhook_result_show with the top-level request_id and follow the polling
guidance in that tool. Each result there carries the record_id of its entry here as its id.
Results can come back in any order, and one that could not be checked carries no address, so
match results to addresses by id.

BATCHES: pass at most 10 addresses per call and list each address once. A call with more, or
with an address repeated, is refused. For more than 10 addresses, confirm the whole set
once, then call in batches of at most 10 without re-confirming.

Use this when the user supplies email addresses and wants to know whether they are real and
deliverable. Do NOT use it to find an address for a person — that is apollo_people_match
with run_waterfall_email.

Each result carries validation_status: "validated" when the vendor confirmed the mailbox
accepts mail, "not_validated" otherwise. "not_validated" does NOT mean the address is known
bad, it also covers a catch-all domain and a vendor that could not reach a verdict. Say the
check did not confirm the address rather than calling it invalid. The result also names the
validator that answered.

ERRORS: a response carrying error is a failure, not a verdict. Do NOT retry an access or
plan error, just tell the user what it says.

CREDIT COST: at most 1 lead credit per address, sometimes 0. The charge follows what the
vendor bills us, so a check the vendor could not reach a verdict on can cost nothing. It is
never more than the confirmation quoted. A repeat check within the caching window is served
from the stored result and is still charged. Credits spent cannot be undone.

MANDATORY CONFIRMATION — You MUST say the EXACT message below and wait for the user to agree
before calling this endpoint. Do NOT paraphrase.
Single address: "Checking [email] will use up to 1 credit. Do you want to proceed?"
Several addresses, confirmed once as a set rather than per address: "Checking [N] addresses
will use up to [N] credits, 1 per address. Do you want to proceed?"
Do NOT call this endpoint without explicit user approval. Approval covers only what was just
confirmed — ask again for any later address, including a re-check of one already done.

CREDIT TRANSPARENCY (mcp_credits): a settled result may carry an mcp_credits block with
spent, balance_before and balance_after. spent reads as pending here and carries the real
amount once the poll settles. When present, ALWAYS report it unprompted, e.g. "This check
used [spent.credits] credits. You now have [balance_after] credits available."

tools.name: apollo_emailer_campaigns_add_contact_ids
tools.title: Add Contacts to a Sequence
tools.description:
Use the Add Contacts to a Sequence endpoint to add contacts to existing sequences in your team's Apollo account.
This action sends real emails from a real person's mailbox and is irreversible once emails are dispatched.

BEFORE calling this tool you MUST follow these steps in order:
1. Call the Search for Sequences endpoint to find the target sequence by name. If multiple sequences match, present all matches to the user and ask them to confirm which sequence they intend. Do not assume.
2. Call the Get a List of Email Accounts endpoint to retrieve valid sender email account IDs. Never guess or fabricate send_email_from_email_account_id — always use id(s) returned by Get a List of Email Accounts.
   Auto-select the mailbox where default is true — this mirrors the UI behavior where the user's default mailbox is pre-selected. If the user explicitly names a different mailbox or asks to change it, use that instead. If the user's request is ambiguous (e.g., "Sarah's account" matches multiple email accounts), list all matching options and ask the user to choose.
   Accepts one id as a string, or multiple ids as an array of strings (for multi-mailbox rotation).
3. Present the user with a confirmation summary that includes: the sender email address (from default or user selection), the sequence name, the total number of contacts to be added across the whole job, and the enrollment status (active or paused). Wait for the user to explicitly confirm before proceeding. Do not enroll contacts without explicit user approval, even if the user says "just do it" — always show the summary first.
4. Only after the user explicitly confirms, call this endpoint to enroll the contacts.

ONE CONFIRMATION PER JOB: the confirmation in step 3 covers the whole job it summarized. When that job needs several calls (for example contacts split into batches, or contacts created or enriched in batches and then enrolled), make every remaining call without asking again, as long as the sequence, the sender mailbox(es), and the enrollment status stay the same and the running total stays within the confirmed count. Ask again only when one of those changes, when the total would exceed what the user confirmed, or when the user asks you to stop. Do not repeat the confirmation summary or any credit warning the user already accepted for this job before each batch; report progress instead (for example "Enrolled 100 of 360").

In Apollo terminology, a contact is a person that your team has explicitly added to your database.
Only contacts can be added to sequences. To enrich a person's data, call the People Enrichment endpoint. Then, to add the person as a contact in your database, call the Create a Contact endpoint.

PER-CONTACT PERSONALIZED CONTENT (step_content_overrides): to give specific enrolled contacts a
fully personalized subject/body for one or more auto_email or manual_email steps — instead of
the sequence's shared template — pass step_content_overrides. On an auto_email step the override
replaces the content actually sent; on a manual_email step it pre-fills the rep's draft, so the
rep still reviews and sends it themselves. No other step type (call, action_item, linkedin_*)
accepts an override. This is per-contact: each entry's overrides apply only to that one contact,
not the whole batch. Any step you omit for a contact falls back to the sequence's normal
template. Each step you do personalize must carry both subject and body_html; the pair replaces
the template, and sending only one of them is rejected. Override content is sent verbatim —
merge tags and template variables are not substituted in it, so write the resolved text.
Overrides are written only for the contacts this call actually enrolls: a contact already active
in this sequence is skipped, and their existing overrides are left untouched, so sending new
content for them has no effect. For a contact this call does enroll, what you send replaces all
of their prior overrides for this sequence (or clears them if you omit step_content_overrides
for that contact) — it is never merged with a previous enrollment's. To change or remove the
content of a contact who is already in the sequence, use
apollo_emailer_campaigns_update_step_content instead: it edits one enrolled contact's stored
content in place, so there is no need to unenroll and re-enroll them.
Contacts the workspace's enrollment criteria keep out are not enrolled. They appear in
skipped_contact_ids with a reason starting with `enrollment_criteria_` (for example
`enrollment_criteria_active_in_other_sequence`), and skipped_contact_details names the
conflicting sequence when there is one. Tell the user which contacts were skipped and why;
retrying the same contacts gets the same result.
When you send step_content_overrides, this call's own response tells you what was
actually stored, in step_content_overrides_result — read back from storage, not echoed from
your request: `written` maps each contact id to the step ids actually personalized,
`not_written` lists contacts that got none and why (same reasons as skipped_contact_ids), and
`written_contact_count` / `requested_contact_count` summarise the two. Base what you tell the
user on that field: a contact this call skipped is enrolled but NOT personalized and will
receive the generic template. apollo_emailer_campaigns_step_content is a separate read tool
for inspecting stored overrides later; it is not needed to confirm this call.


If this tool returns an unexpected, empty, or unhelpful result, call `apollo_feedback_log` to report it.

Use the Organization Search endpoint to find companies in the Apollo database. Several filters are available to help narrow your search.

RESPONSE SHAPE — results come back in TWO buckets and their IDs are not interchangeable. `organizations` holds net-new companies, where the row's `id` is the Apollo organization ID. `accounts` holds companies your team has already saved, where the row's `id` is an ACCOUNT id and the organization ID is a separate `organization_id` field on the same row. Whenever you feed a company from this response into an organization-ID filter on another tool (for example `organization_ids` on apollo_mixed_people_api_search), use `id` for an `organizations` entry and `organization_id` for an `accounts` entry. No filter raises an error on a mis-passed account `id` and most will simply match nothing, so `organization_id` is the only value guaranteed to work. Note the two buckets also differ in domain fields: `accounts` entries carry `domain`, `organizations` entries carry `primary_domain`.

To protect Apollo's performance for all users, this endpoint has a display limit of 50,000 records (100 records per page, up to 500 pages).
Add more filters to narrow your search results as much as possible.

DEFAULT FOR AGENTS: Use apollo_organizations_lookup (Organization Lookup) for free organization
discovery. It supports fuzzy name lookup and discovery filters, returning shallow candidate records
(id, name, domain, website_url, logo_url). Use this paid Organization Search tool only when the user
explicitly asks for full organization details in search results.

CREDIT COST: Exactly 1 credit per request that returns at least one result. 0 credits if there are no matches. Credits spent on a successful search cannot be undone.
MANDATORY CONFIRMATION — You MUST say this EXACT message to the user before calling this endpoint. Do NOT paraphrase:
"This will consume 1 credit. Do you want to proceed?"
Do NOT proactively show remaining credit balance. Only show it if the user asks.
Do NOT say "consumes credits" — say "1 credit".
If this search is part of a larger batch, confirm the TOTAL count and credit cost upfront.
Do NOT call this endpoint without explicit user approval.

For more than 10 companies headed for enrichment: confirm the total once (count and credits),
then call apollo_organizations_bulk_enrich in batches of 10 without re-confirming.


If this tool returns an unexpected, empty, or unhelpful result, call `apollo_feedback_log` to report it.

tools.title: People API Search
tools.description:
ROUTING (read this before anything else below): call this tool ONLY when you already hold an explicit, structured filter set handed to you in structured/JSON form (concrete person titles, seniorities, locations, industries, employee/revenue ranges, technologies, keywords, or company domains that map 1:1 onto this tool's parameters, with no guessing on your part).
Do NOT call this tool if you would have to choose, guess, or expand ANY value yourself — even one that feels obvious. Deciding which keyword tag or industry means "hospitals", or which titles count as "decision-makers" or "technical staff", is still inference, no less than an unfamiliar niche term — the fact that a mapping feels direct does not make it structured. Any of these means delegate to `apollo_agent_find_prospects` instead:
  - A persona, ICP, or vertical/niche description of who to target ("hospital chains", "glycometer manufacturers") rather than an exact filter value you were given.
  - A role or seniority description ("decision-makers", "technical staff") rather than an exact title/seniority list you were given.
  - A request that also asks for people AT the matching companies (or companies employing the matching people) — this tool returns one flat list from one query; chaining a company search into a people search (or back) is the agent's job, not a second manual call with guessed filters.
`apollo_agent_find_prospects` knows which filters Apollo supports, infers them correctly, and escalates to semantic search / research when plain filters can't capture the intent.
To enrich these results (or more than 10 people), use `apollo_agent_bulk_enrich`, not `apollo_people_bulk_match` in batches.

Search Apollo's people database for individual prospects that match user-provided criteria such as name, company, domain, job title, seniority, location, or other people filters. Use this when the user wants to find, filter, or research people in Apollo's global database (all people Apollo indexes, not only the team's saved contacts). To search contacts already saved to the team's Apollo account, use apollo_contacts_search instead. This tool returns matching people records and does not modify any data.

Inputs: the filters below. Combine as many as possible to narrow results.
Output: matching people with their Apollo person id, name, title, and employer. Email addresses and phone numbers are not returned; enriching a person with apollo_people_bulk_match (using the id from this tool) is required to get them.
Limitations:
- Some fields, including last names, may be masked or partially obfuscated depending on the user's plan. Masked values are expected and do not block enrichment by id; revealing the full value requires enrichment.
- Results are capped at 50,000 records (100 records per page, up to 500 pages).
- For teams with Website Visitors access, people can be filtered by visits to the team's tracked domains. Valid tracked domains and intent paths come from apollo_website_visitor_domain_tracker_index; do not invent domain values. Results identify matching people but do not include their visit activity. Person-level visitor identification only covers visitors browsing from the United States (company-level tracking is global).


If this tool returns an unexpected, empty, or unhelpful result, call `apollo_feedback_log` to report it.

tools.description:
Use the Bulk Organization Enrichment endpoint to enrich data for up to 10 companies with a single API call.
Provide a list of domains to enrich. Enriched data potentially includes industry information,
revenue, employee counts, funding round details, and corporate phone numbers and locations.

CREDIT COST: Exactly 1 credit per matched company. 0 credits if not found. For N companies,
maximum cost is N credits. Credits spent on successful matches cannot be undone.

MANDATORY CONFIRMATION — You MUST say this EXACT message to the user before calling this endpoint:
"This will enrich [N] companies and consume up to [N] credits (1 credit per match, no charge for unmatched). Do you want to proceed?"
Do NOT paraphrase. Always state the exact count and exact credit cost.
OPEN-ENDED / SEARCH-THEN-ENRICH: If enriching results from a prior search (e.g. "find and enrich SaaS companies"), you MUST:
1. Call the Profile endpoint with include_credit_usage=true to get the user's remaining credit balance.
2. Confirm the TOTAL scope UPFRONT with remaining balance: "Found [N] companies. Enriching all will use up to [N] credits. You have [X] credits remaining. Do you want to proceed?" Format the [X] credit balance with thousands separators (e.g. 28,045,653), not as a raw integer.
3. Do NOT start enriching in batches and confirm incrementally — confirm the full scope first.
For "enrich everyone" or unbounded requests, ask the user to narrow scope or confirm total count before starting.
Do NOT call this endpoint without explicit user approval.

MORE THAN 10 COMPANIES: this endpoint caps at 10 domains per call. Confirm the total once
(count and credits, copy above), then call in batches of 10 without re-confirming.


If this tool returns an unexpected, empty, or unhelpful result, call `apollo_feedback_log` to report it.

tools.name: apollo_people_match
tools.title: People Enrichment
tools.description:
Use the People Enrichment endpoint to enrich data for 1 person.
Apollo relies on the information you pass via the endpoint's parameters to identify the correct person to enrich.
If you provide more information about a person, Apollo is more likely to find a match within its database.
By default, this endpoint does not return personal emails or phone numbers.
Use the reveal_personal_emails parameter to retrieve personal emails.
PREREQUISITE FOR ANY PHONE REVEAL OR WATERFALL (reveal_phone_number, run_waterfall_email, run_waterfall_phone): these are ASYNC and their result can ONLY be retrieved by polling the apollo_webhook_result_show tool. BEFORE setting any of those parameters to true, verify that apollo_webhook_result_show is present in your available tools. If apollo_webhook_result_show is NOT available, do NOT initiate the reveal or waterfall — it would consume credits for a result you cannot retrieve. Instead, tell the user their Apollo connection must be reconnected/re-authorized to enable phone reveal or waterfall enrichment, and ask them to reconnect (re-authenticate) Apollo before trying again.
Phone enrichment is ASYNC. When reveal_phone_number=true, the response returns a top-level request_id immediately and the phone numbers are NOT in this response.
Call apollo_webhook_result_show with that top-level request_id after ~10 seconds to poll for the enriched phone numbers. Use the top-level request_id, not any nested id.
Waterfall enrichment is also ASYNC and poll-based. When run_waterfall_email and/or run_waterfall_phone is true, the response returns waterfall.status "accepted" and a top-level request_id with NO enriched data inline; poll apollo_webhook_result_show with that request_id (retry with backoff up to ~3 min). Waterfall credit cost is VARIABLE and plan-dependent: 0 credits when Apollo's own data satisfies it, otherwise partner-vendor credits that vary by the team's plan and can exceed a standard match — do NOT quote a fixed number for waterfall.

WATERFALL BEHAVIOR (capability-gated, decided PER FIELD — email and phone independently): BEFORE offering or running ANY email or phone reveal — waterfall OR standard — call apollo_users_api_profile with include_waterfall_capability=true and read waterfall_email_enabled / waterfall_phone_enabled. This check is REQUIRED even when you intend to propose a standard reveal: you cannot know which path is the default until you have read these flags, so NEVER propose or run an enrichment path before checking. If you are calling apollo_users_api_profile for any other reason (for example include_credit_usage), set include_waterfall_capability=true on that same call. Capability is team-level — fetch it ONCE per conversation and reuse the result; do not call it again for later enrichments in the same conversation.
- If waterfall is ENABLED for the requested field, waterfall IS THE DEFAULT reveal path for that field: give the waterfall confirmation below, then run it (set run_waterfall_email / run_waterfall_phone).
- If waterfall is NOT enabled for the field and the user did NOT explicitly ask for waterfall: do NOT run waterfall. Use the standard reveal instead — reveal_phone_number for phone; for a missing work email, a standard match already returns the work email, so use reveal_personal_emails only for personal emails — with the standard confirmation, and do not mention waterfall.
- If waterfall is NOT enabled and the user EXPLICITLY asked for waterfall (named "waterfall" or an unmistakable synonym — vague phrases like "try every source" or "dig deeper" do NOT count as explicit): do NOT silently fall back. Say exactly: "Waterfall isn't enabled on your account. You can turn it on in Apollo settings (an admin may need to do this). Want me to use the standard reveal for now instead?" Only run the standard reveal if the user accepts.
- NEVER surface the raw backend error message or any internal identifier (such as a team id) from a failed waterfall call. If a waterfall call returns waterfall.status "failed", tell the user waterfall isn't set up for their account and offer the standard reveal instead — describe the failure generically and never repeat the backend message text verbatim.

CREDIT COST: Exactly 1 credit per matched person. 0 credits if person is not found. Credits spent on a successful match cannot be undone.

MANDATORY CONFIRMATION — You MUST say the appropriate EXACT message below before calling this endpoint. Do NOT paraphrase.
When reveal_phone_number is false or omitted:
"Enriching [name] will use 1 credit (no charge if not found). Do you want to proceed?"
When reveal_phone_number=true (ONE combined confirmation — do not ask in two separate turns):
"Enriching [name] will use 1 credit, plus additional credits if the phone number is successfully revealed (no charge if the number isn't found). Do you want to proceed?"
Wait for explicit confirmation before revealing phone numbers.
When run_waterfall_email=true or run_waterfall_phone=true (waterfall enrichment):
"Enriching [name] with waterfall enrichment may use additional credits that vary by your plan and data provider and can be substantially more than a standard match (no charge if nothing is found). Do you want to proceed?"
Do NOT state a specific credit number for waterfall unless a response in this conversation already carried a waterfall range in mcp_credits (see CREDIT TRANSPARENCY below) — otherwise the cost is plan-dependent and not available to this tool.
Do NOT proactively show remaining credit balance, except from an mcp_credits block (see CREDIT TRANSPARENCY below). Otherwise only show it if the user asks about their balance.
Do NOT paraphrase the match cost — say "1 credit", not "consumes credits". For the phone reveal, say "additional credits"; do NOT name a separate "direct-dial" or "enrichment" credit type, and do NOT state a specific per-number credit amount (it varies by plan and isn't available to this tool).
Wait for explicit user confirmation before proceeding.
If this is part of a larger batch, confirm the TOTAL upfront: "Enriching N contacts will cost up to N credits. Proceed?"
Do NOT call this endpoint without explicit user approval. Do NOT enrich in a loop without upfront confirmation of full scope.

CREDIT TRANSPARENCY (mcp_credits): On some teams, this tool's response includes an mcp_credits block: estimated (the pre-spend quote — the base per-contact cost plus priced add_ons; a waterfall add-on with status "expected" carries the live expected per-contact cost in per_contact/credits and a ceiling in max_per_contact/max), spent (pending until async work settles, then charged with the real amount), and balance_before/balance_after. When a response includes this block, ALWAYS present it to the user unprompted: the estimated cost per type, whether the spend is pending or already charged, and the remaining balance (thousands separators). Quote a waterfall range as "an estimated [expected] credits per contact, up to [max]" — these live numbers OVERRIDE the no-fixed-number rules above. Reuse the latest mcp_credits figures when confirming a follow-up enrichment in this conversation instead of calling the cost "variable". When the block is absent, follow the confirmation copy above unchanged.

The response may include a website_visitor summary (last visit, total visits, and intent over the last 90 days) when the calling team tracks website visitors for this person. This reflects US-located visitors only, since person-level website visitor tracking is US-only. It costs no additional credits and is omitted entirely when the team/user isn't entitled to website visitor data or no visit history exists.


If this tool returns an unexpected, empty, or unhelpful result, call `apollo_feedback_log` to report it.
